question.worked_solution:
First, note that $x=-8$ and $x=\frac{5}{2}$ cannot be solutions since division by $0$ is undefined.

To solve the equation, we first apply cross-multiplication:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{x+8} & =\frac{3}{5-2x} \\ 2\cdot (5-2x) & =(x+8)\cdot 3 \\ 10-4x & =3x+24\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we apply the addition and multiplication principles, as usual:

$$
\begin{aligned}10-4x & =3x+24 \\ 10-4x+4x & =3x+24+4x \\ 10 & =7x+24 \\ 10-24 & =7x+24-24 \\ -14 & =7x \\ \frac{-14}{7} & =\frac{7x}{7} \\ -2 & =x\end{aligned}
$$

Since $x=-2$ is different from $x=-8$ and $x=\frac{5}{2},$ we can accept it as a solution. Therefore, the solution is $x=-2.$
